why: A (universes at 0) is theorem_10_4_5 plus twelve supporting lemmas. theorem_10_4_5 says Φ_* and Φ^* are mutually inverse bijections Γ ⇄ Γ'; when |Φ| = |Ψ|, Φ_* = Ψ_* and Φ^* = Ψ^*; and both restrict to Γ⁺. The project docstring says the Fred part is not formalized. B has this content as (a)–(f), with B's choice-based pushB/pullB, and adds (g): Φ_* and Φ^* map Fred(P, μ) ⇄ Fred(P', μ'). A says nothing about Fred, so A_to_B fails at (g). That is a genuine omission, not glue. The missing piece is the invariance of StrongBundle.IsScFredholmSection under local strong bundle isomorphisms, and the project's docstring notes it lacks this. Everything else holds: A_to_BnoFred proves A ⇒ (B without (g)) through the non-item bridges pullB = h.pullback (pullback_eq) and pushB = h.pushforward ((10.22) pushforward_eq). B_to_A gets theorem_10_4_5 from (a)–(f); Φ^* = Ψ^* comes from Φ_* = Ψ_* and the inverse laws. It also gets isScSmoothSection_pushforward from (a), isScPlusSection_pushforward from (f), and bijOn_pushforward_example from these. The other nine conjuncts are general lemmas B does not state: pull-backs of non-functorial sections, the local form exists_pushforward_local, and M-polyfold and strong-bundle-iso lemmas. They were re-proved outright by copying the project's proofs, which use non-item lemmas.
B_issue: The blind statement includes the Fred restriction (g), as quoted. The item title says 'without the Fred part'; the blind author noticed this and kept (g) as a separate conjunct. So the A_to_B failure is the project's announced omission, not a misreading of B.
